title: SEO Guide for Dentists: The Complete 2026 Local Playbook
summary: From Google Business Profile to schema, this SEO Guide for Dentists shares 2026-ready local tactics to rank, earn reviews, and drive calls. Start today.
body_text: Welcome to your complete SEO guide for dentists. If you feel like your dental practice is invisible online, you’re in the right place. Local Search Engine Optimization, or SEO, is the process of making your practice show up when potential patients in your neighborhood search for a dentist. With nearly everyone turning to Google to find local services, mastering SEO is no longer optional; it’s essential for a steady flow of new patients. Direct Answer: How do dentists improve their local SEO in 2026? To rank a dental practice in 2026, you must optimize for three core pillars: Google Business Profile (GBP) Prominence (categories, reviews, and proximity), Topical Authority (detailed service pages with FAQ schema), and Trust Signals (verified patient testimonials and high-speed mobile performance). Practices that combine accurate NAP data with consistent, high-quality video content and structured data (Schema) are 75% more likely to appear in Google’s AI Overviews and the Local Map Pack. This SEO guide for dentists will walk you through everything you need to know, from the basics of your Google Business Profile to advanced strategies for content and link building. It might seem like a lot, but understanding these concepts will empower you to attract more local patients. And if it feels overwhelming, remember there are services like Rankai’s done for you SEO program that can handle it all, letting you focus on what you do best: patient care. Local SEO Overview for Dentists Local SEO is all about optimizing your online presence to attract more patients from relevant local searches. For a dentist, this means making sure your practice appears when someone nearby searches for “dentist near me” or “dental clinic in [Your City].” It involves improving your visibility in Google’s Map Pack (the map and three business listings at the top of local results) and in the regular organic search results. Since 46% of all Google searches have local intent , being visible locally is critical. Importance of Local SEO for Dentists Why is local SEO so important? It directly connects you with high intent patients in your community. When someone has a toothache, they aren’t just browsing; they’re looking for a solution right now. Consider that 99% of consumers have used the internet to find information about a local business in the last year . If your practice isn’t showing up, you’re missing out on nearly all of them. These searchers act fast, too. A staggering 76% of people who search for a nearby business on their smartphone visit one within a day . For dentists, this translates directly into more calls, appointments, and patients walking through your door. Google Business Profile Optimization Your Google Business Profile (GBP) is the cornerstone of your local SEO. It’s the free listing that appears in Google Maps and the Map Pack, showing your practice name, address, phone number, hours, and reviews. Optimizing it means filling out every single section with accurate, keyword rich information. A complete profile makes your business appear 2.7 times more reputable to customers . Key steps include choosing the right categories, writing a compelling description, adding your services, and uploading plenty of high quality photos. This is the single most valuable part of any local SEO guide for dentists. NAP Consistency and Citation Management NAP stands for Name, Address, and Phone number. NAP consistency means ensuring this information is listed in the exact same format across every online platform, from Google and Yelp to dental specific directories. Citations are mentions of your business online. Managing them is crucial because Google cross references this data to verify your legitimacy. Inconsistent information can confuse search engines and erode patient trust. In fact, 73% of consumers lose trust in a local business when they find conflicting information online . Online Review Management Online reviews are the modern word of mouth. Your strategy should involve proactively asking happy patients for reviews, monitoring feedback across platforms like Google and Yelp, and responding to every review. Reviews heavily influence patient decisions, with 76% of consumers trusting online reviews as much as personal recommendations . A strong rating is non negotiable; 57% of consumers will only consider a business if it has four or more stars . Responding to reviews, both good and bad, shows you care and can build significant trust. On Page SEO for a Dental Website On page SEO involves optimizing the content and HTML of your website to be search engine friendly. Use an on-page SEO checklist to make sure titles, headings, and meta data are handled consistently. For your dental site, this means having dedicated pages for each service (like cleanings, implants, Invisalign), using local keywords in page titles and headings, and writing unique meta descriptions, while making sure you avoid keyword stuffing . A logical site structure with internal links per page planned intentionally (for example, linking from your dental implants page to your bone grafting page) is also key. Experts agree that having a dedicated page for each service is one of the most impactful factors for ranking well, a critical takeaway from this SEO guide for dentists. Local Keyword Research Before you can optimize your site, you need to know what your potential patients are searching for. Local keyword research is the process of finding these terms. Start by building a keyword cluster to group related dental topics and map them to pages. It goes beyond “dentist in [Your City].” You’ll want to find phrases like “emergency dentist open Saturday,” “kids dentist [Neighborhood],” or “Invisalign cost [City].” Pay special attention to “near me” searches, which have exploded in popularity. This research forms the foundation of a smart local SEO strategy, ensuring the rest of this seo guide for dentists is applied effectively. Location Specific Content Creation Creating content tailored to your specific geographic area helps you connect with the local community and strengthens your SEO. This could mean creating individual pages for each office location or service area you cover, complete with local testimonials and driving directions. You can also write blog posts with a local angle, like “How [Your City]’s Summer Festivals Can Affect Your Smile.” This signals to Google that you are an active part of the community. In one study, a brand that created city specific landing pages saw a massive 1,132% increase in new users . Service Page Optimization for Patient Intent Each page on your website describing a service, like teeth whitening or root canals, should be optimized for patient intent. This means anticipating and answering the questions a potential patient has when they land on that page. What is the procedure? How much does it cost? What is the recovery like? Providing clear, comprehensive answers not only helps convert visitors into patients but also allows you to naturally include relevant keywords. Well optimized service pages are a critical component of any dental SEO plan and a core principle in this SEO guide for dentists. Schema Markup for Dentists and Local Businesses Schema markup is a type of code you add to your website to help search engines understand your content more deeply. If you’re new to structured data, start with this guide to author schema to understand how entities and credibility signals work. For a dental practice, you can use Dentist or LocalBusiness schema to label your name, address, phone number, hours, and even patient reviews. This can make you eligible for rich snippets in search results, like star ratings or FAQ dropdowns appearing directly under your listing. As search becomes more driven by AI, providing this kind of structured data is becoming increasingly important. Mobile Optimization Your website must look great and function perfectly on a smartphone. Google uses a mobile first index, meaning it primarily ranks your site based on its mobile version. A huge portion of local searches happen on mobile devices, and these searchers are ready to take action. Critically, 61% of mobile searchers are more likely to contact a local business if it has a mobile friendly site . Ensure your text is readable, buttons are easy to tap, and your site loads quickly. A slow or clunky mobile experience will send potential patients straight to your competitors. Hyperlocal and Location Page Strategy A hyperlocal strategy focuses on targeting very specific geographic areas, like a single neighborhood or zip code. This is often done by creating dedicated location pages for each office or distinct community you serve. Each page should feature unique content relevant to that area, such as photos of the local office, testimonials from neighborhood patients, and information on nearby landmarks. This approach helps you dominate search results for the patients who are physically closest to your practice. Website Content Strategy for Dentists A content strategy is your plan for publishing useful, relevant information that attracts and engages potential patients. This includes a mix of detailed service pages and informational blog posts that answer common questions (e.g., “Braces vs. Invisalign: Which is Right for You?”). Creating helpful content positions you as a trusted authority in oral health. Plan clusters that build topical authority around core treatments like implants, Invisalign, and emergency care. It also allows you to target a wide range of keywords that patients search for at different stages of their journey. A service like Rankai can supercharge this by consistently creating and optimizing dozens of content pieces each month. Building Expertise (E-E-A-T) Google’s "Your Money or Your Life" (YMYL) guidelines are strictly applied to dental sites. To rank, you must prove you are a medical authority: Detailed Bios: Include NPI numbers, board certifications, and professional memberships (e.g., ADA). Medical Review: If a staff member writes a blog post, add a "Medically Reviewed by [Doctor Name]" tag at the top. Case Studies: Use "Before and After" galleries with descriptions of the clinical challenge and the solution to demonstrate real-world experience. Measuring Local SEO Success (Calls, Directions, Bookings) How do you know if your SEO is working? You need to track the actions that matter. Here’s how to tell if your SEO strategy is working and which signals to watch. Success isn’t just about traffic; it’s about new patient inquiries. Key metrics to measure include: Phone Calls: How many calls did your Google Business Profile and website generate? Direction Requests: How many people clicked for directions to your office? This is a strong signal of intent to visit. Online Bookings: How many appointments were scheduled through your website’s contact form or booking tool? An increase in these actions is a clear sign your local SEO efforts are paying off. 2026 Dental SEO Performance Benchmarks Metric 2026 Target Goal Why It Matters GBP Interaction Rate > 5% High clicks for directions/calls signal relevance to Google. Page Load Speed Under 2.5 Seconds Essential for "Core Web Vitals" and mobile ranking. Review Velocity 2-5 New Reviews / Month Consistency is now more important than total volume. Organic Click-Through > 3% High CTR tells Google your meta titles match patient intent. Common Local SEO Mistakes Many dental practices make avoidable errors that hurt their online visibility. Some of the most common mistakes include: Not claiming or fully optimizing your Google Business Profile. This is a massive missed opportunity. Having inconsistent Name, Address, and Phone (NAP) information across different websites. Ignoring online reviews or responding unprofessionally to negative feedback. Having a website that is not mobile friendly. Thinking of SEO as a one time task. It requires ongoing effort to maintain and improve rankings. AI Search and Generative Engine Optimization Considerations The rise of AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Google’s Search Generative Experience is changing how people find information; review Google’s AI Overview to understand how these summaries may impact dental search visibility. While traditional search isn’t going away, optimizing for these new platforms is wise, and this SEO guide for dentists will prepare you for what’s next. This means having well structured, authoritative content that an AI can easily understand and use to answer a user’s question. Clear FAQ sections, detailed service pages, and schema markup all help. Your Google Business Profile and patient reviews are also key data sources that AI may pull from, making their accuracy and quality more important than ever. Align Website Listing and GBP Signals Your website and your Google Business Profile should tell the same story. This alignment means ensuring your name, address, phone number, hours, and services are perfectly consistent between the two. Google uses your website to verify the information in your GBP, so any discrepancy can create confusion and weaken your SEO. Link your GBP to the most relevant page on your site (usually the homepage or a location page) and make sure that page reinforces all the key details of your practice. Photo and Media Optimization for Trust High quality photos and videos are powerful tools for building trust. A Google Business Profile with compelling images of your office, your team, and your technology will always outperform one with no photos. In fact, businesses with photos on their GBP receive 42% more requests for driving directions and 35% more clicks through to their websites . Use professional photos of your clean, welcoming office and friendly staff to make a great first impression and encourage potential patients to take the next step. Leveraging Video for Local Authority In 2026, video is no longer a "nice-to-have." Google frequently pulls short-form video clips directly into search results for queries like "how does Invisalign work?" The 30-Second FAQ: Record yourself answering one common patient question per week. Office Tours: A 15-second "walk-in" video helps anxious patients feel comfortable before they arrive. Video Testimonials: Written reviews are great, but a video of a smiling patient is the ultimate trust signal for AI search engines looking for "authentic experience." Social Media Strategy for Local Visibility While social media isn’t a direct ranking factor, it plays a vital role in local visibility and brand awareness. An active presence on platforms like Facebook and Instagram helps you connect with your community, share patient testimonials, and drive traffic to your website. Your social profiles also rank in Google, helping you control more of the search results for your practice name. It’s another way to show you are an active, engaged, and trusted local business. Backlink and Local Link Building Backlinks are links from other websites to yours. Google views them as votes of confidence. Local link building focuses on earning links from other reputable websites in your area, such as the local chamber of commerce, community blogs, or news sites. Sponsoring a local charity event or being featured in a news story are great ways to earn these powerful local links, which signal to Google that your practice is a prominent and trusted part of the community. GBP Category and Service Selection Choosing the right categories in your Google Business Profile is absolutely critical. Your primary category (e.g., “Dentist,” “Cosmetic Dentist,” or “Orthodontist”) has a massive impact on the searches you show up for. In fact, experts consider the primary GBP category the number one ranking factor for the local Map Pack . Be as specific and accurate as possible, and use additional categories to cover all your main specialties. Then, fill out the “Services” section with a detailed list of every treatment you offer. Accurate Location and Service Area Setup Your physical address is a cornerstone of local SEO. You must ensure your address is listed correctly on your GBP and that the pin is placed accurately on the map. Google heavily weighs proximity, so if its data about your location is wrong, you won’t show up for nearby searches. For a typical dental practice where patients visit you, your verified address is all you need. The “service area” feature is generally for businesses that travel to their customers, so most dentists should leave it blank to ensure their address remains visible. Responding to Reviews Professionally and Safely How you respond to reviews is almost as important as the reviews themselves. Always respond to both positive and negative feedback. For positive reviews, a simple thank you is enough. For negative reviews, respond professionally, empathetically, and without violating patient privacy (HIPAA). A thoughtful response can turn a negative situation into a positive impression for future patients who see that you take feedback seriously. A remarkable 80% of consumers are more likely to use a business if they see it responds to reviews . Monitoring and Updating Content SEO is not a one and done task. A key part of any ongoing seo guide for dentists is monitoring your website’s content and keeping it fresh and accurate. Regularly update service pages with new information, add new team member bios, and refresh old blog posts. Google rewards websites that show signs of life and provide up to date information. This ongoing effort can be time consuming, which is why many practices turn to a continuous service. For instance, Rankai not only creates new content but constantly rewrites underperforming pages until they rank, ensuring your website never becomes stale. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) 1. How long does local SEO take to show results for a dental practice? While you can see some quick wins from optimizing your Google Business Profile, significant results from a comprehensive local SEO strategy typically take 3 to 6 months. SEO is a long term investment that builds momentum over time. 2. What is the most important part of this SEO guide for dentists? If you only have time for one thing, focus on your Google Business Profile. Claim it, fill out every section completely and accurately, upload at least 10 high quality photos, and start actively gathering patient reviews. It provides the biggest impact for the least amount of effort. 3. Can I do dental SEO myself or should I hire an agency? You can certainly implement many of the basics from this guide yourself. However, a consistent, high level strategy that involves content creation, technical SEO, and link building requires significant time and expertise. Many dentists find that hiring an expert or using a service allows them to get better results while they focus on patient care. 4. How much should I budget for local SEO? Costs can vary widely depending on your market’s competitiveness and the scope of work. Some agencies charge thousands per month. Newer, more efficient models like Rankai’s flat monthly program offer a comprehensive and affordable alternative designed to provide a clear return on investment without long term contracts. 5. How do I get more patient reviews on Google? The best way is to ask! Create a simple process to ask happy patients for a review at the end of their appointment. You can also send a follow up email or text message with a direct link to your Google review page to make it as easy as possible for them.

Clinical research, which operates at the intersection of scientific complexity, regulatory rigor, and compliance, is undergoing a similar shift 1. Much of the public conversation around digital transformation in clinical research centers on artificial intelligence, decentralized trials, and advanced analytics. Yet one of the most significant shifts has occurred in operations: how samples are tracked, how patients move through complex workflows, how investigational products are managed, and how data flows across stakeholders. As trials become increasingly global, decentralized, and data-intensive, operational excellence has evolved from a supporting function to a strategic differentiator. The transition to a digitally enabled ecosystem represents a structural rethinking of how trials are planned, executed, monitored, and scaled. Patient Engagement and Adherence Medication adherence remains one of the biggest challenges that pharmaceutical companies deal with 2 and the issue is often amplified during decentralized clinical trials. When patients are dispersed across geographies and interacting with sites remotely, monitoring adherence becomes both more difficult and more critical to study integrity. Smart packaging technologies have emerged as a practical solution. By integrating sensors, data capture, and digital identifiers directly into packaging formats such as vials and auto-injectors, sponsors can gain visibility into dosing behavior, tampering events, and environmental conditions. Technologies such as RFID and Bluetooth-enabled monitoring allow real-time or near-real-time data capture, improving both patient engagement and operational oversight. These solutions are robust and scalable and can be cost-effective when deployed in various common form factors. In one recent implementation, a leading pharmaceutical company 3 deployed smart packaging technology to evaluate its impact on patient engagement and overall trial efficiency. The results demonstrated how connected packaging can support adherence monitoring while reducing manual intervention and data gaps. Simplifying Clinical Trials Operations Clinical trials today are markedly more complex than they were two decades ago. Precision medicine, biomarker-driven eligibility criteria, adaptive protocols, and global site networks have increased both logistical and regulatory demands. Rare disease trials, for example, often require intricate sample handling, time-sensitive processing, and multi-layered data reconciliation across borders. Common operational challenges include: Multi-country regulatory variation Fragmented technology stacks Manual data entry and reconciliation Delays in biological sample processing Patient drop-off due to logistical burden Limited real-time visibility into site performance Digital transformation has the potential to address these through integrated systems, automation, and real-time transparency. When systems are connected end-to-end – from site workflows to central labs to sponsors – data silos shrink and error rates decline. Improving Efficiency As clinical trials have evolved in size, scope and complexity, operational strain has increased. Yet many workflows still rely on manual processes and fragmented communication. For example, specimen management remains a particular vulnerability, with risks ranging from lost samples to temperature excursions affecting sensitive materials. Established technologies such as RFID tagging offer enhanced durability and automated data capture compared to traditional barcodes and QR codes. Recent advancements in Bluetooth-enabled labels now integrate environmental sensors capable of monitoring temperature, humidity, and other critical parameters – particularly important for condition-sensitive drugs and biological samples. Leveraging these technologies for real-time tracking improves chain-of-custody visibility and enables more seamless data exchange among sites, logistics providers, laboratories, and sponsors. When combined with AI-driven analytics, these systems can identify bottlenecks proactively, enabling corrective action before delays escalate. Product Logistics Operational transformation extends beyond data and samples to investigational product logistics. Modern digital supply chain systems now support: Real-time temperature monitoring Automated resupply triggers Smart packaging tracking Geofenced shipment alerts These capabilities reduce drug wastage, support Good Clinical Practice (GCP) compliance, and minimize last-minute resupply emergencies. Integration with patient scheduling platforms further aligns supply availability with visit timing, reducing research site burden and improving coordination. Product Labeling and Accessibility Digitalization is also reshaping product labeling. Enhanced labels can now incorporate spoken audio and custom text with the tap of a smartphone , haptic feedback, and high-contrast text, expanding accessibility across diverse patient populations. In decentralized trials, where patients often self-administer treatments at home, accessible labeling can significantly improve usability and adherence. Conventional technologies such as Optical Character Recognition (OCR), when integrated with AI, further enhance accessibility by enabling digital reading, translation, and interaction features – strengthening both inclusivity and data integrity. Building the Digital Backbone of Clinical Research As clinical trials become more global, decentralized, and data-driven, complexity is unlikely to diminish. What is changing is how that complexity is managed. A well-designed digital transformation strategy – grounded in integrated infrastructure rather than isolated tools – can streamline operations, enhance patient experience, and reduce workflow burden. Technologies such as RFID and Bluetooth-enabled tagging form part of a scalable foundation for modern trial execution. When combined with intelligent analytics, these systems move organizations from reactive problem-solving to proactive optimization. Operational bottlenecks will always exist within research ecosystems. But with deliberate deployment of connected technologies and automation, sponsors can reduce inefficiencies, improve data quality, and strengthen the economics of innovation. title: The Ultimate Guide to Commercial Refrigeration Maintenance for Restaurants Nathalie Schrans Nathalie Schrans March 11, 2026
summary: Discover expert tips for commercial refrigeration maintenance to extend equipment life and prevent breakdowns across restaurant locations.
body_text: In This Post 1. Stay on Top of Regular Preventative Maintenance (PM) 2. Train Staff to Perform Basic Checks and Regular Cleaning 3. Avoid Overloading and Poor Placement 4. Prioritize Critical Equipment 5. Proactively Manage Warranty and Repair Costs 6. Build a Reliable Vendor Network 7. Plan for Critical Failures 8. Use Software for Maintenance Tracking Simplify Commercial Refrigeration Maintenance with OpenWrench A refrigeration failure in a busy restaurant can derail operations, spoil inventory, and rack up costly repairs. For facilities managers overseeing multiple locations, keeping systems in top condition is critical — but where do you start? We spoke with Danny Koontz of Windy City Equipment , a seasoned expert with decades of experience in restaurant facilities management and equipment repair, to get his top tips on commercial refrigeration maintenance. These best practices will help you extend equipment lifespans, prevent breakdowns, and save time. After reading our guide, you’ll learn how to: Prevent equipment failures and reduce downtime with preventative maintenance schedules Train staff to perform basic checks can catch issues before they escalate Avoid common mistakes like overloading and poor placement Use tools like facilities management software to simplify maintenance tracking and vendor coordination 1. Stay on Top of Regular Preventative Maintenance (PM) Without consistent preventative maintenance (PM) , small problems like a dirty coil or a torn gasket can grow into major failures. “Do your PM quarterly if you can,” says Danny. “Many people will skip PM as a cost-cutting measure. But you need at least two or three visits per year.” During PM visits, a service technician should: Check for leaks Inspect and replace worn gaskets Check door seals Inspect and adjust door hinges Clean condenser and evaporator coils Check and replace air filters Inspect fan motors Inspect and tighten electrical connections Test and calibrate thermostats Check that temperatures are consistent Test door heaters for walk-in units Check refrigerant levels Use tools like OpenWrench to track completed PM visits, technician notes, and upcoming schedules. Make sure every visit includes a checklist of completed tasks and that the technician signs it. See preventative maintenance schedules for all your locations with OpenWrench. You can quickly edit, pause, skip, or move up PM visits in one place. Plus, all previous and active work orders are linked to each location for easy access. 2. Train Staff to Perform Basic Checks and Regular Cleaning Your staff plays a vital role in keeping refrigeration systems running smoothly between regular maintenance services. Equipping them with basic inspection and cleaning skills allows you to catch small problems early and avoid costly emergency service calls . “When PM companies aren’t there, it falls on the restaurant to clean and do routine maintenance,” says Danny. “It’s like having a maid who comes to your home once a month. That’s not the only time it gets cleaned. It has to be done in between too.” Every week, your location staff should: Monitor temperatures at least once a day, first thing in the morning and at scheduled times throughout the day Check for leaks and water puddles under or around units Listen for unusual noises, like grinding or humming sounds, from compressors or fans Clean condenser coils, door seals, fans, and vents Look for cracks or tears in door gaskets Wipe down interior and exterior surfaces Check for frost buildup To help your staff succeed, develop an easy-to-follow guide for daily, weekly, and monthly checks. Include tasks like temperature logs, gasket inspections, and coil cleaning reminders. Platforms like OpenWrench make it simple to share these maintenance checklists across multiple locations, ensuring consistency. Staff can also quickly record their checks and report any issues they find. Keep the instructions straightforward and prioritize tasks that anyone can do. “They just need to do simple things, like take the front screen off a refrigeration unit and check if it’s clean,” Danny explains. OpenWrench lets your location staff log daily refrigerator temperature checks right from their mobile device. This gives you access to refrigeration metrics across all locations so you can proactively monitor their performance and schedule service visits before they break down. 3. Avoid Overloading and Poor Placement Proper placement and loading are critical for refrigeration performance. Blocking vents or placing units near heat sources, like fryers, reduces efficiency. Overloading, especially during busy times, can freeze up units. “Coolers are built to accommodate what they have,” Danny explains, “but when you stack product to the ceiling, there’s no airflow.” These mistakes often go unnoticed until they cause a failure during a critical time. Here’s how to optimize your equipment placement and loading: Conduct regular site surveys: Check that refrigeration units are positioned away from ovens, griddles, fryers, and other hot equipment and have enough space around them for proper airflow. Designate loading zones: Mark areas inside walk-ins where products should and shouldn’t be stored to avoid overcrowding key airflow zones. Consider climate control: Keep units in well-ventilated, temperature-controlled areas. Avoid placing units in spaces prone to high humidity or temperature spikes, which can strain the cooling system. 4. Prioritize Critical Equipment Not all refrigeration systems impact operations equally. While losing a stand-up freezer isn’t catastrophic, downtime for a walk-in cooler can halt service. Walk-in coolers, prep table refrigeration, and line equipment are often essential for daily operations. Losing one of these units can lead to food spoilage, lost revenue, and unhappy customers, so they need to be a top priority when failures occur. Below are our tips for protecting your most critical refrigeration equipment: Create a response hierarchy: Rank your refrigeration units by how essential they are to operations. Units tied to food storage and preparation should be at the top of the list, while less-used equipment (like secondary freezers) can wait longer for repairs. Conduct regular risk assessments: Identify which units are most likely to fail based on age, condition, and usage. Focus your PM on these systems to reduce the chances of downtime. Establish rapid repair protocols: Partner with trusted vendors and negotiate service agreements that prioritize these units during emergencies. 5. Proactively Manage Warranty and Repair Costs “If the restaurant manager doesn’t tell their vendor a piece of equipment is or might be under warranty, it often gets missed,” says Danny. “Then the restaurant loses money because they’re paying to fix a problem when it’s still under warranty.” Here’s how to manage your warranties effectively: Digitize your warranty records: Store warranty details in a centralized digital system, such as OpenWrench, so they’re easy to access during service calls. Include purchase dates, coverage terms, and serial numbers for each piece of equipment. Train staff to flag warranty repairs: Teach managers and staff to always check for warranty coverage before authorizing repairs. A simple reminder can save significant costs. Track repair histories: Maintain detailed service records for each unit, noting what was repaired, when, and by whom. This helps determine whether the issue is warranty-eligible or recurring. Not sure whether your equipment is still under warranty? See warranty management in action in OpenWrench 6. Build a Reliable Vendor Network Working with the right service providers reduces downtime, ensures quality repairs, and keeps your equipment in peak condition. But not all vendors are created equal, and finding the right fit for your needs requires careful vetting. “When you’re getting ready to pick a company, ask them how many cold-side techs they have,” Danny advises. “Because every tech may only be versed in hot side, cold side, or HVAC. Or a vendor might have 20 techs total but only five cold-side techs.” Below are our best practices for building your vendor network: Ask for references: When comparing vendors, always ask them for a list of restaurant companies they’re working with, then call those facilities managers. This will help you discover potential issues before you work with them. Check performance and responsiveness: Choose vendors with a proven track record of reliability and timely service. Test their responsiveness during the vetting process by noting how quickly they answer questions or provide estimates. Leverage technology to manage vendors: Use platforms like OpenWrench to track vendor schedules, monitor performance, and consolidate invoices. A centralized system helps ensure you’re consistently working with the best providers across all locations. 7. Plan for Critical Failures No matter how well you maintain your commercial refrigeration systems, they will still fail unexpectedly. But not all failures have the same impact. While some units can wait for repair, others, like walk-ins or prep table coolers, are essential for daily service. Preparing ahead of time helps you avoid panicked decisions and costly repairs. Danny recalls a restaurant with daily deliveries in anticipation of higher volume during the Daytona 500. Food was stacked to the ceiling in the walk-in, blocking airflow and making the unit freeze up. The freezer’s door heater was also broken, which caused frost buildup that made the door nearly impossible to open. The solution came too late: renting an additional freezer unit. “The next year, we planned ahead,” Danny says. “We got a rental freezer and put it in the parking lot to handle the overflow.” Here’s how you can plan for equipment failures: Map critical vs. non-critical equipment: In your contingency plans, prioritize systems essential to your daily operations, like walk-ins and prep tables. Identify temporary solutions: For critical equipment, explore backup options like portable refrigeration units or storing items at a nearby location, before emergencies happen. Document backup protocols: Create detailed plans for each critical system, including who to contact, where to source temporary equipment, and step-by-step instructions for minimizing downtime. “If you’re prepared, you don’t panic,” Danny emphasizes. “That’s how you keep things moving even when something goes wrong.” 8. Use Software for Maintenance Tracking Facilities management software helps streamline the process so everything is organized and no maintenance tasks fall through the cracks. “If PM is done correctly, I will get notes for anything that needs to be repaired,” explains Danny. “If two days after a PM visit the equipment is down, I may call the service company and say, ‘PM was just done on Monday, and everything was fine. You sure you didn’t miss something?’” A computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) makes tracking these notes easy so you can hold vendors accountable and ensure no detail gets missed. Here’s how to use this software to simplify your refrigeration maintenance: Report and track issues: Use software to document problems as soon as they occur. This creates a record for reference and ensures issues are addressed promptly. Approve and track work orders: With platforms like OpenWrench, you can view, approve, and track work orders across all your locations to monitor vendor performance and repair timelines. Receive PM alerts: Set automated reminders for upcoming PM visits to ensure critical tasks like coil cleaning or temperature checks aren’t overlooked. Analyze maintenance data: Review historical data to identify patterns, such as recurring issues with specific equipment or vendors. This helps prioritize repairs and make smarter budgeting decisions. title: Stevanato Group Delivers 7% Revenue Growth (9% at Constant Currency) for Fiscal Year 2025, Including Record Revenue from High-Value Solutions and Expanded Margins
body_text: Stevanato Group Delivers 7% Revenue Growth (9% at Constant Currency) for Fiscal Year 2025, Including Record Revenue from High-Value Solutions and Expanded Margins March 04, 2026 6:30am EST Download as PDF Related Documents Audio Earnings Webcast 20-F Filing PDF HTML XBRL ZIP HTML Prepared Comments PDF - Establishes Fiscal 2026 Guidance - PIOMBINO DESE, Italy--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Stevanato Group S.p.A. (NYSE: STVN), a leading global provider of drug containment, drug delivery, and diagnostic solutions to the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, and life sciences industries, today announced its financial results for the fourth quarter and full year 2025. Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Highlights (comparisons to prior-year periods) For the fourth quarter of 2025, revenue increased 5% (7% on a constant currency basis) to €346.5 million, and high-value solutions represented 49% of total revenue. Gross profit margin increased 120 basis points to 30.9%, and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 70 basis points to 28.2%, for the fourth quarter of 2025. Diluted earnings per share were €0.17, and adjusted diluted earnings per share were €0.18 for the fourth quarter of 2025. For the fiscal year 2025, revenue increased 7% (9% on a constant currency basis) to €1.186 billion, and high-value solutions represented 46% of total revenue. Gross profit margin increased 160 basis points to 29.0%, and adjusted EBITDA margin increased 160 basis points to 25.1% for the fiscal year 2025. For the fiscal year 2025, diluted earnings per share grew 19% to €0.51, and adjusted diluted earnings per share increased 13% to €0.54. The Company is establishing its fiscal 2026 guidance. The Company expects revenue in the range of €1.26 billion to €1.29 billion, adjusted EBITDA in the range of €331.8 million to €346.9 million, and adjusted diluted EPS in the range of €0.59 to €0.63. Fourth Quarter 2025 Results For the fourth quarter of 2025, total revenue increased 5% year-over-year (7% on a constant currency basis) to €346.5 million, driven by a 10% (13% on a constant currency basis) revenue increase from the Company's Biopharmaceutical and Diagnostic Solutions (BDS) Segment, which offset the anticipated revenue decline from the Engineering Segment. Revenue from high-value solutions increased 31%, year-over-year, to a record €171.4 million, representing 49% of total revenue for the fourth quarter of 2025. In the fourth quarter of 2025, strong performance in the BDS Segment led to a 120 basis-point increase in gross profit margin to 30.9%, compared with the same period last year, and operating profit margin was 20.2%, consistent with the same period last year. Net profit was €47.6 million, with diluted earnings per share of €0.17, for the fourth quarter of 2025, and adjusted net profit was €49.8 million with diluted earnings per share of €0.18. For the fourth quarter of 2025, adjusted EBITDA increased to €97.7 million, and the adjusted EBITDA margin improved 70 basis points to 28.2%, compared with the same period last year. Franco Stevanato, Chief Executive Officer, commented, "We concluded fiscal year 2025 with another solid quarter that led to positive full‑year performance underpinned by strong top-line growth, a favorable mix of high value solutions, and expanded margins. Biologics remain an important tailwind and in 2025 GLP1s represented approximately 19% to 20% of total Company revenue. There’s no doubt that we have been successful in winning our fair share of the GLP1 market. This success is rooted in our long history of being a trusted partner to customers, our global footprint which provides supply chain security, and the quality of our products which have characteristics that resonate with our customers." Biopharmaceutical and Diagnostic Solutions (BDS) Segment Revenue grew 10% (13% on a constant currency basis) to €307.1 million for the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with the same period last year, driven by a 31% increase from high-value solutions to €171.4 million, which represented 56% of BDS Segment revenue. Revenue from other containment and delivery solutions decreased 9% to €135.7 million, compared with the same period last year, due to a decline in certain lower-value bulk products, as the Company transitions to a larger portfolio of high-value products aligned with its strategic investments. For the fourth quarter of 2025, gross profit margin increased 50 basis points to 31.6%, and operating profit margin rose 50 basis points to 23.8%, compared with the same period last year, driven by: (i) a favorable mix of high value solutions, (ii) improvements as the Company scales commercial production in its new facilities, which remain dilutive to the corporate margin, and (iii) an improved vial market which led to higher vial production and better utilization. These positive trends were partially offset by the unfavorable impact from foreign currency translation and tariffs. Engineering Segment As expected, revenue from the Engineering Segment decreased 23% to €39.4 million for the fourth quarter of 2025, compared with the same period last year, driven by lower revenue from our glass converting and assembly lines businesses. For the fourth quarter of 2025, gross profit margin for the Engineering Segment decreased 280 basis points to 15.8%, compared with the same period last year, and continued to be impacted by an unfavorable project mix and a lower volume of new work. Balance Sheet and Cash Flow As of December 31, 2025, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of €130.6 million, and net debt of €337.7 million. For fiscal year 2025, capital expenditures totaled €294.9 million, as the Company continues to increase capacity in its new manufacturing facilities in Indiana and Italy. Cash flow from operating activities for fiscal year 2025 was €286.1 million. Cash used for the purchase of property, plant, and equipment, and intangible assets totaled €275.1 million. Increased operational cash flow and reduced capital expenditures resulted in €18.4 million of positive free cash flow for the year ended 2025. The Company believes that it has adequate liquidity to fund its strategic priorities over the next twelve months through a combination of cash on hand, cash generated from operations, available credit lines, and the ability to access additional financing. 2026 Guidance The Company is establishing its fiscal 2026 guidance and expects: Revenue in the range of €1.26 billion to €1.29 billion; Adjusted EBITDA in the range of €331.8 million to €346.9 million; and Adjusted diluted EPS in the range of €0.59 to €0.63. Franco Stevanato, Chief Executive Officer, concluded, "We enter 2026 with positive momentum and a clear focus on disciplined execution. We operate in attractive, growing end markets with favorable secular tailwinds. Innovation across the industry continues to advance patient care and we remain mission critical to the delivery of innovative biologics. Biologics are expected to remain our fastest growing end market and a key driver to top-line growth and margin expansion as we continue to move up the value chain. In Latina and Fishers, we expect to increasingly benefit from improved utilization, efficiencies, and operating leverage, as we support our customers with quality and reliability." The authorization is effective immediately, has no time limit, and may be modified, suspended or discontinued at any time. “We are pleased that the Board has authorized a new $125 million stock repurchase program, reflecting confidence in our long-term growth strategy, superior underwriting capabilities and robust capital position,” said Bruce Lucas, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Slide. “Given the abundant capital we maintain to successfully execute on our diversified growth strategy and the ability of our business model to generate significant free cash flow, we will opportunistically repurchase common stock when we believe it is below fair value and further create long-term value for our shareholders. At current levels, we believe it is very accretive for Slide to repurchase common stock.” Under the prior completed program, Slide repurchased 7,109,417 common shares at a weighted average share price of $16.88. Share repurchases under the stock repurchase program may be made in the open market at prevailing market prices, through privately negotiated transactions, or through other structures in accordance with applicable federal securities laws, at times and in amounts as management deems appropriate. The timing and the amount of any common stock repurchases will be determined by the Company’s management based on its evaluation of market conditions, the company’s liquidity needs, corporate and regulatory requirements and restrictions, share price, trading volume and other factors. Repurchases of common stock may be made under a Rule 10b5-1 plan, which would permit common stock to be repurchased when the company might otherwise be precluded from doing so under insider trading laws. The repurchase program does not obligate the company to purchase any particular number of shares and may be suspended, modified, or discontinued at any time without prior notice. body_text: At Greif, we believe that sustainability and business performance go hand in hand. A great example of this is our work with sustainable financing, a tool that rewards companies for improving their sustainability performance, and the value it creates for our customers, suppliers, and communities. What is sustainable financing? Sustainable financing refers to financial arrangements, such as loans, that are linked to a company’s sustainability performance. If the company meets defined environmental, social, or governance (ESG) targets, it can receive more favorable financial terms. In short: the better the sustainability performance, the better the financing conditions. Using EcoVadis to Measure Performance To track progress, Greif relies on EcoVadis, one of the most trusted global sustainability rating platforms. EcoVadis evaluates companies across environmental impact, labor and human rights, ethics, and sustainable procurement, and issues a score that reflects overall sustainability performance. Our Sustainable Financing Journey In 2022, Greif signed a sustainable financing agreement that linked our loan pricing to achieving a targeted EcoVadis score. Once we reached that target, we unlocked meaningful financial benefits for the company. These savings strengthen our ability to reinvest in our operations, enhance our sustainability programs, and increase the value we deliver to our customers and suppliers. Why this Matters This year, Greif renewed its sustainable financing agreement, which now extends through 2031 and remains tied to our EcoVadis performance. As our score continues to improve, so does our potential to unlock additional financial benefits, further reinforcing the connection between strong sustainability performance and positive business results. Sustainable financing is more than a financial mechanism — it reflects Greif’s long-term commitment to responsible growth. For customers: Improved sustainability performance enhances supply chain resilience and supports your own ESG goals. For suppliers: It underscores our shared commitment to responsible sourcing and ethical business practices. For communities: Better sustainability performance contributes to reduced environmental impact and stronger social responsibility. Greif’s sustainable financing work demonstrates that doing the right thing for the environment and society can also drive stronger business results. By continuously improving our sustainability performance, we reinforce operational strength, build stakeholder trust, and contribute to a more sustainable future. Non-GAAP Financial Measures: One Liberty computes FFO in accordance with the “White Paper on Funds from Operations” issued by the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts (“NAREIT”) and NAREIT’s related guidance. FFO is defined in the White Paper as net income (calculated in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles), excluding depreciation and amortization related to real estate, gains and losses from the sale of certain real estate assets, gains and losses from change in control, impairment write-downs of certain real estate assets and investments in entities where the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity. Adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures are calculated to reflect FFO on the same basis. In computing FFO, management does not add back to net income the amortization of costs in connection with its financing activities or depreciation of non-real estate assets. Since the NAREIT White Paper does not provide guidelines for computing AFFO, the computation of AFFO may vary from one REIT to another. One Liberty believes that FFO and AFFO are useful and standard supplemental measures of the operating performance for equity REITs and are used frequently by securities analysts, investors and other interested parties in evaluating equity REITs, many of which present FFO and AFFO when reporting their operating results. FFO and AFFO are intended to exclude GAAP historical cost depreciation and amortization of real estate assets, which assumes that the value of real estate assets diminish predictability over time. In fact, real estate values have historically risen and fallen with market conditions. As a result, management believes that FFO and AFFO provide a performance measure that when compared period-over-period, should reflect the impact to operations from trends in, among other things, occupancy rates, rental rates, operating costs and interest costs, without the inclusion of depreciation and amortization, providing a perspective that may not be necessarily apparent from net income. Management also considers FFO and AFFO to be useful in evaluating potential property acquisitions. FFO and AFFO do not represent net income or cash flows from operating, investing or financing activities as defined by GAAP. FFO and AFFO are not alternatives to net income as a reliable measure of One Liberty’s operating performance nor an alternative to cash flows as measures of liquidity. FFO and AFFO do not measure whether cash flow is sufficient to fund all of our cash needs, including principal amortization, capital improvements and distributions to stockholders. title: The New Hatch: Leading the AI CSR Era
summary: Why we rebuilt our website and brand, and what it took to represent the complete AI CSR platform for service businesses.
body_text: Service businesses are under more pressure than ever. Whether an independent operator building toward a sale, a multi-location brand managing complexity across markets, or a PE-backed business delivering returns to investors, the math is the same: grow revenue and protect margins. AI is reshaping that equation, but as the market floods with AI point solutions, the gap between tools and infrastructure has never been wider. And it's become increasingly clear that Hatch is that infrastructure, which is why we rebuilt our brand from the ground up. Here's the story behind it. The evolution of Hatch Chris Bache and Bill Violante founded Hatch in 2018 to give service teams a better way to engage with customers. What started as an outsourced service has evolved into the leading AI CSR platform for service businesses — spanning voice, SMS, and email, with deep integrations into the tools and partners this industry relies on every day. In January 2026, Yelp acquired Hatch for approximately $270 million, a validation of the platform, the team, and the category we've helped define. As one customer put it, "Getting acquired by a brand as established as Yelp is a strong signal that the home services space is getting more attention, more investment, and more innovation. That is good news for all of us." With that kind of momentum, it was imperative that our website reflected where Hatch stands today: the definitive AI CSR platform built for every channel, every stage, and every role in service operations. A brand to match the platform An acquisition of this scale doesn't happen without serious product depth and traction. Here's what's behind it. At the end of the day, what matters to service businesses is top line and bottom line. How much revenue are you generating from your appointments and sales, and how much does it cost to get there? That's true whether you're a growing single-location business or a national brand managing dozens of markets. In this industry, leads can run $150–$200+ each,* and that's cost per lead alone. When you factor in what it takes to actually convert that lead — the follow-up, the staffing, the coordination — customer acquisition costs climb to $250–$350+.* And that still doesn't account for what comes after: the appointment confirmations, the job updates, the invoicing, the review requests, the re-engagement campaigns to drive repeat business and memberships. Meanwhile, the teams doing this work face 38% annual turnover* and cost one half to two times their annual salary to replace.* Revenue alone isn't the whole picture. It's what you keep after all is said and done. Hatch exists to move both numbers in the right direction. Our AI CSRs handle inbound calls, respond to leads in seconds, follow up on estimates, re-engage aged leads and past customers, and manage customer communication across voice, SMS, and email, all from one platform. The result is more booked appointments, higher close rates, and a customer experience that scales without ballooning headcount or operational complexity. The businesses using Hatch today are seeing 3x higher set rates on digital leads, 80% reduction in manual CSR workload, and $80K+ in annual operational savings per AI agent. That's the difference between AI as a tool and AI as infrastructure: revenue up, operational costs down. Inside the rebuild To do the platform justice, that meant restructuring our site from the ground up to reflect the depth and scale of what Hatch has become. Here's what that looks like. The breadth of a full platform. A few pages wasn't enough to capture what Hatch's AI agents deliver across the entire customer journey. So we created dedicated pages for each of our seven core capabilities and seven core solutions, plus a platform overview that shows how they all come together. Sophisticated, but not complicated. Service businesses have intricate operations, and the Hatch platform is designed to bring order to that complexity. Our new navigation follows the same principle, with dedicated pages that help you quickly find the solutions, integrations, and use cases that match your business. Voice AI, front and center. Hatch is at the forefront of voice AI in this space, handling both inbound and outbound calls as a part of a robust, multi-channel approach. On the new site, you can hear it in action, talk to it yourself, and explore how Hatch integrates with the tools already in your tech stack. Customers everywhere. One of the things we're most proud of is the depth of customer relationships we've built over the years, and the new site brings much more visibility to those success stories throughout. Because the best proof of what Hatch can do for growth and margins is the businesses already seeing it. Every detail is intentional. Hatch isn't a point solution you bolt onto your operations. It's AI infrastructure embedded into your workflows, your systems, and your customer journey. That takes rigorous implementation, true expertise, and a solutions engineering team dedicated to understanding the complexities in every client's business. The site is built with that same level of care. The road ahead This new look reflects not just where Hatch is today, but where we're headed. In fact, one of our biggest priorities was building a site that could keep pace with a product that's evolving fast, making it easy to bring new capabilities to light without losing the bigger picture. Because that's what it takes when you're building the AI infrastructure that will power the next generation of service businesses. And we'll keep investing in the platform, the product, and the partnerships that make that possible. title: 5 virtual office benefits for remote teams

Increased employee engagement and retention rates Remote team isolation is still a problem many distributed workforces face. When new teams pilot Gather, they often refer to internal engagement surveys or retention metrics to gauge if Gather is making an impact. After using Gather, employee retention improved by 70% . Of course, a virtual workspace platform like Gather won’t fix your company’s attrition issues on its own. However, it gives your remote team a place to put strong company values into action. Instead of an isolating work environment, you have a shared place to engage the team. ‍ “I've seen a drastic shift in attitude in terms of how happy the team is to actually show up on work, as well as the level of collaboration that the team is doing as part of their day to day tasks.” ‍ Robert O., CTO via G2 Customer Example: Weme, an innovation agency in Brazil, began surveying employees weekly to gauge their happiness with work. With Gather, instead of relying on scheduled interactions, you can simply walk up to someone’s desk or Wave them over if you want to talk. The result? You can reduce meeting fatigue and have more natural conversations.
